title: Selective suppression of electronic orders via interlayer coupling in superconducting bilayer nickelate thin films
authors: Ziao Han, Lifen Xiang, Tianren Wang, Congcong Le, Jun Zhan, Siyi Lei, Sonia Francoual, Qisi Wang, Jiangping Hu, Tao Xiang, Ronny Sutarto, Xianxin Wu, X. J. Zhou, Zhihai Zhu
abstract: The discovery of spin-density-wave (SDW) order in bilayer nickelates has intensified interest in its interplay with superconductivity. Unlike cuprates, where doping rapidly suppresses the Néel temperature, the SDW transition temperature ($T_{\mathrm{SDW}}$) in bilayer nickelates is robust against oxygen annealing and even increases under pressure. Here, we combine oxygen annealing with isovalent rare-earth ($A$-site) substitution to effectively apply $c$-axis uniaxial pressure, realizing superconducting bilayer nickelate films with $T_{\mathrm{SDW}}$ suppressed from 150 K to 70 K. Notably, while SDW order is weakened but remains, a second charge-like anisotropy order is completely eliminated in the superconducting state. Polarization-resolved O $K$-edge X-ray absorption and electronic structure calculations show that strengthened interlayer coupling reconstructs the Fermi surface and weakens the SDW. These findings, consistent with a spin-spinless stripe ground state, provide new insight into the mechanism of density wave formation and their interplay with superconductivity.
summary: This paper uses X-ray scattering and spectroscopy to study how tuning the interlayer coupling in superconducting nickelates selectively suppresses one electronic order (charge-like anisotropy) while weakening another (SDW). The findings suggest that these competing orders are governed by distinct energy scales, offering new insights into the mechanism of high-temperature superconductivity in these materials.
main_problem: The study investigates the complex interplay between superconductivity and competing electronic orders, specifically Spin-Density Wave (SDW) and charge-like anisotropy order, in bilayer nickelate thin films.
main_result: The research demonstrates that enhancing interlayer coupling, via oxygen annealing or A-site substitution, selectively suppresses the charge-like anisotropy order while weakening but retaining the SDW order.
method: The work combines advanced experimental techniques, including polarization-resolved O K-edge X-ray absorption and Resonant Elastic X-ray Scattering (REXS), with theoretical electronic structure calculations.
model_or_system: The physical system is superconducting bilayer nickelate thin films (e.g., $	ext{La}_{2-x}	ext{Pr}_x	ext{Ni}_2	ext{O}_{7-\delta}$), whose electronic properties are tuned by controlling oxygen stoichiometry and applying strain via rare-earth substitution.
key_observables: SDW transition temperature ($T_{	ext{SDW}}$), charge-like anisotropy order signal (via $\sigma$-polarization REXS), and interlayer hybridization strength (via O K-edge XAS).
important_parameters: Interlayer coupling strength, oxygen content ($\delta$), and applied uniaxial pressure (mimicked by A-site substitution).
main_assumptions: The observed phenomena are consistent with a spin-spinless stripe ground state, and the tuning mechanisms (annealing/substitution) effectively control the interlayer coupling.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the temperature dependence of SDW and charge-like order signals under varying oxygen content and substrate conditions, confirming the selective suppression mechanism.
paper_structure: The paper systematically presents measurements showing how tuning the interlayer coupling (via annealing or substitution) differentially affects the SDW and charge-like orders, linking these changes to Fermi surface reconstruction.
why_interesting: The selective suppression of different competing orders by tuning structural parameters (interlayer coupling) provides a concrete model for understanding how competing instabilities govern the superconducting dome in strongly correlated nickelates.
